Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

just adverb

exactly

also exactly, precisely, the very, very (the very one), just then, just as

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.23.4: eā ipsā hōrā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 3.21: trīgintā diēs erant ipsī, it was just thirty days (Lewis & Short)

ipse, ipsa, ipsum

pronoun, declension

the very, just, exactly

Latin puts the “just” on the word it marks: id ipsum, just that; tum ipsum, just then; nunc ipsum, right now, at this very moment (Cic. Att. 7.3.2, Lewis & Short); with numbers, exactly.

Other words

  • cum maximē (tum maximē) — just as; just then

    also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.142: haec cum maximē loquerētur, just as he was saying this (Lewis & Short); Traupman 87: just as, cum maximē; just then, tunc maximē; Traupman 335

    nunc cum maximē, right now, at this very time (Cic. Sen. 38, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē

    there my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthdayCic. Att. 4.1.4

  • Salvum tē advenīre, Dēmea, gaudēmus. — Ehem, opportūnē: tē ipsum quaeritō.

    We’re glad to see you safely here, Demea. — Ah, good timing: you’re just the man I’m looking for.Ter. Ad. 80–81

  • ōlim mihi nūllās epistulās mittis. nihil est, inquis, quod scrībam. at hoc ipsum scrībe, nihil esse quod scrībās

    you haven’t sent me a letter for ages. ‘There’s nothing to write,’ you say. Then write just that: that there’s nothing to writePlin. Ep. 1.11.1

See also just now, only, moment.
